text: Algebra of vectors. We've seen some properties of vectors from section 2.1.5, properties of vectors, where there are a few other properties not yet mentioned. A vector can be reversed, that is, multiplied by a scalar negative 1, nullified, made equal. To reverse the direction of a vector, we follow the rules for scaling a vector. Vector A equals negative A sub X i hat minus A sub Y j hat minus A sub Z k hat. The number zero can be generalized to vector algebra through the object called the null vector, denoted by vector zero. It represents a vector that has no length or direction. Vector zero equals zero i hat plus zero j hat plus zero k hat. If the difference of two vectors, vector A and vector B, is set to the null vector, we have vector A minus vector B equals zero i hat plus zero j hat plus zero k hat equals vector A. Vector zero equals A sub X minus B sub X i hat plus A sub Y minus B sub Y j hat plus A sub Z minus B sub Z k hat. By matching components, we can see that A sub X minus B sub X equals zero, or A sub X equals B sub X. A sub Y minus B sub Y equals zero, or A sub Y equals B sub Y. A sub Z minus B sub Z equals zero, or A sub Z equals B sub Z. When vector A minus vector B equals vector zero, this implies that vector A equals vector B because all their corresponding components are equal. The full table, choosing a vector method, is available on the course webpage. Example problem, military convoy direction. The problem, a military convoy advances through unknown territory. In a Cartesian coordinate system, the unit vector i hat denotes geographic east, j hat denotes geographic north, and k hat denotes altitude above sea level. The convoy's velocity is given by vector V equals 4.0 i hat plus 3.0 j hat plus 0.1 k hat kilometers per hour. If the convoy were forced to retreat, in what geographic direction would it be moving? Describe both its horizontal direction and its vertical motion. The model. We model the convoy's motion using a three-dimensional velocity vector expressed in Cartesian components. The horizontal motion occurs in the east, north plane, while the vertical motion is represented by the k hat component. A retreat corresponds to reversing the direction of motion. Therefore, the new velocity vector must be anti-parallel to the original velocity vector. This means the new velocity vector points in the opposite direction, but retains the same relative component ratios. The math. The original velocity vector is vector V equals 4.0 i hat plus 3.0 j hat plus 0.1 k hat kilometers per hour. The positive k hat component shows that the convoy is ascending. Since 0.1 kilometers per hour equals 100 meters per hour, the convoy is climbing while it moves horizontally toward the northeast. The horizontal direction of the original motion is determined from the ratio of the northward component to the eastward component. Theta equals tan to the power of negative 1 of V sub y over V sub x is equal to tan to the power of negative 1 of 3.0 over 4.0 is approximately equal to 37 degrees. The original horizontal motion is therefore 37 degrees north of east. For a retreat, the new velocity must point opposite the original velocity. A vector anti-parallel to vector V can be written as vector U equals minus alpha vector V, where alpha is a positive scale factor. Choosing the same speed corresponds to alpha equals 1, so the retreat velocity is vector U equals negative 4.0 i hat minus 3.0 j hat minus 0.1 k hat kilometers per hour. The negative k hat component shows that the convoy would be descending during the retreat. The horizontal components are both negative, so the retreat direction lies southwest. The reference angle is theta equals tan to the power of negative 1 of 3.0 over 4.0 is approximately equal to 37 degrees. The convoy therefore retreats at an angle of 37 degrees south of west while descending. The descending motion follows from the negative k hat component of the reversed velocity vector, analytical vector addition. Resolving vectors into their scalar components allows us to use vector algebra to find sums and differences of vectors without using graphical methods, that is analytically. For example, to find the resultant of two vectors, vector A and vector B, we simply add them relative to their components. Component matching rule. Vectors can only be added or subtracted by combining matching components. i hat components combine only with i hat. J hat components combine only with j hat. K hat components combine only with k hat. For example, 3 i hat plus 2 j hat plus 5 i hat minus j hat equals 8 i hat plus j hat. But expressions like 3 i hat plus 2 j hat plus 5 k hat cannot be simplified further because none of the subscripts match. If the subscripts do not match, the components represent different directions and cannot be combined. Vector addition by components is accomplished as follows. Vector R equals vector A plus vector B equals A sub X plus B sub X i hat plus A sub Y plus B sub Y j hat plus A sub Z plus B sub Z k hat. And analytical methods can be used to find the result of many vectors by combining them by components. For example, if we sum up n vectors, vector F sub 1 dot dot dot vector F sub n, where each vector F sub n equals F sub n X by 1, equals F sub n X i hat plus F sub NY j hat plus F sub N Z k hat. The resultant vector is vector F sub R equals vector F sub 1 plus vector F sub 2 plus dot dot dot plus vector F sub n equals sum sub n equals 1 to the power of n vector F sub n. So, this is the resultant vector F sub R equals sum sub n equals 1 to the power of n parentheses F sub n X i hat plus F sub NY j hat plus F sub N Z k hat parentheses. The resultant vector is defined as vector F sub R equals F sub RX i hat plus F sub R Y j hat plus F sub R Z k hat, where F sub RX equals sum sub N equals 1 to the power of n F sub n X equals F sub 1 X plus F sub 2 X plus dot dot dot dot. Plus F sub N X F sub R Y equals sum sub N equals 1 to the power of n F sub NY equals F sub 1 Y plus F sub 2 Y plus dot dot dot plus F sub NY. F sub R Z equals sum sub N equals 1 to the power of n F sub N Z equals F sub 1 Z plus F sub 2 Z plus dot dot dot plus F sub N Z. Checkpoint, pause and check your understanding. A vector sum contains A sub X, B sub Y and C sub X, which terms can be combined. The Python code is available on the course web page. Example problem, vector addition component wise, the problem, three displacement vectors, vector A, vector B and vector C lie in the horizontal plane. Their magnitudes are A equals 10.0 centimeters, B equals 7.0 centimeters, and C equals 8.0 centimeters. And their direction angles measured counterclockwise from the positive X axis are alpha equals 35 degrees, beta equals negative 110 degrees, and gamma equals 30 degrees respectively. So, solve each vector into its Cartesian components and determine the following. A vector R equals vector A plus vector B plus vector C, B vector D equals vector A minus vector B, C vector S equals vector A minus three vector B plus vector C. The model, we model each displacement as a two-dimensional vector in the X, Y plane. Each vector is described by a magnitude and a direction angle, so each one can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components. Vector addition and subtraction are performed by combining matching components only. Once the components of a resultant are known, the resultant can be written in unit vector form. The math. Each vector is resolved into rectangular components before the vector combinations are evaluated. For any vector V with magnitude V and direction angle theta measured from the positive X axis, the components are V sub X equals V cos theta, V sub Y equals V sine theta. Applying these component definitions to vector A gives A sub X equals A cos alpha equals 10.0 cos 35 degrees equals 8.19 centimeters. A sub Y equals A sine alpha equals 10.0 sine 35 degrees equals 5.73 centimeters. Applying the same component definitions to vector B gives B sub X equals B cos beta equals 7.0 cos 110 degrees equals negative 2.39 centimeters. B sub Y equals B sine beta equals 7.0 sine 110 degrees equals negative 6.58 centimeters. Applying the same component definitions to vector C gives C sub X equals C cos gamma equals 8.0 cos 30 degrees equals 6.93 centimeters. C sub Y equals C sine gamma equals 8.0 sine 30 degrees equals 4.00 centimeters. A for the vector sum vector R equals vector A plus vector B plus vector C matching components are added to form the components of the resultant vector. R sub X equals A sub X plus B sub X plus C sub X equals 8.19 minus 2.39 plus 6.93 equals 12.73 centimeters. R sub Y equals A sub Y plus B sub Y plus C sub Y equals 5.73 minus 6.58 plus 4.00 equals 3.15 centimeters. The vector sum in component form is therefore vector R equals 12.7 i hat plus 3.1 j hat centimeters. B for the vector difference vector D equals vector A minus vector B. The components of vector B are subtracted from the corresponding components of vector A. D sub X equals A sub X minus B sub X equals 8.19 minus minus 2.39 equals 10.58 centimeters. D sub Y equals A sub Y minus B sub Y equals 5.73 minus 6.58 equals 12.31 centimeters. The vector difference in component form is therefore vector D equals 10.6 i hat plus 12.3 j hat centimeters. C for the combination vector S equals vector A minus 3 vector B plus vector C. The components of vector B are first multiplied by 3 and then subtracted component by component. S sub X equals A sub X minus 3 B sub X plus C sub X equals 8.19 minus 3 times negative 2.39 plus 6.93 equals 22.29 centimeters. S sub Y equals A sub Y minus 3 B sub Y plus C sub Y equals 5.73 minus 3 times negative 6.58 plus 4.00 equals 29.47 centimeters. The vector combination in component form is therefore vector S equals 22.3 i hat plus 29.5 j hat centimeters. The conclusion. The analytical component method gives vector R equals 12.7 i hat plus 3.1 j hat centimeters. Vector D equals 10.6 i hat plus 12.3 j hat centimeters. And vector S equals 22.3 i hat plus 29.5 j hat centimeters. These results show that vector addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication can all be handled by combining matching X and Y components. The problem. Four dogs named Astro, Balto, Clifford, and Doug play a tug of war game with a toy. We define East as the positive X direction and North as the positive Y direction. Astro pulls with a force of magnitude A equals 160.0 N at an angle alpha equals 55 degrees south of East. Balto pulls with a force of magnitude B equals 200.0 N at an angle beta equals 60 degrees east of North. Clifford pulls with a force of magnitude C equals 140.0 N at an angle gamma equals 55 degrees west of North. Doug pulls on the toy in such a way that the toy does not move. What force must Doug apply, magnitude and direction, in order to keep the toy in equilibrium? The figure is shown on the course web page. The model. We model each dog's pull on the toy as a force vector in the horizontal plane. The positive X direction points East and the positive Y direction points North. Each force is described by a magnitude and a direction, so each pull can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components. The toy remains at rest only if the vector sum of all forces acting on it is zero. Doug's force must therefore balance the combined pull of the other three dogs. This means Doug's force must have the same magnitude as that combined force but point in the opposite direction. The math. The direction descriptions are first converted into standard direction angles measured counterclockwise from the positive X axis. Astro pulls south of East, Balto pulls East of North and Clifford pulls west of North. So their direction angles are theta A equals negative 55 degrees. Theta B equals 90 degrees minus 60 degrees equals 30 degrees. Theta C equals 90 degrees plus 55 degrees equals 145 degrees. The next force is resolved into X and Y components using the magnitude and direction angle of that force. A sub X equals A cos theta A equals 160.0, cos negative 55 degrees equals plus 91.8 nuutens. B sub Y equals A sine theta A equals 160.0 sine negative 55 degrees equals negative 131.1 nuutens. B sub X equals B cos theta B equals 200.0, cos 30 degrees equals plus 173.2 nuutens. B sub Y equals B sine theta B equals 200.0 sine 30 degrees equals plus 100.0 nuutens. C sub X equals C cos theta C equals 140.0, cos 145 degrees equals negative 114.7 nuutens. C sub Y equals C sine theta C equals 140.0 sine 145 degrees equals plus 80.3 nuutens. The resultant force from astro, balto, and Clifford is found by adding matching components. R sub X equals A sub X plus B sub X plus C sub X equals 91.8 plus 173.2 minus 114.7 equals 150.3 nuutens. R sub Y equals A sub Y plus B sub Y plus C sub Y equals negative 131.1 plus 100.0 plus 80.3 equals plus 49.2 nuutens. The resultant force from the first three dogs is therefore Vector R equals 150.3 i hat plus 49.2 j hat nuutens. For the toy to remain at rest, Doug's force must cancel the resultant force from the other three dogs. Therefore, Doug's force is the opposite of Vector R. Vector D equals negative 150.3 i hat minus 49.2 j hat nuutens. The magnitude of Doug's force is found from the components of Vector D. D equals the square root of negative 150.3 squared plus negative 49.2 squared nuutens. equals 158.1 nuutens. The reference angle for Doug's force is found from the ratio of the magnitudes of the southward and westward components. Theta equals 10 to the power of negative 1 of 49.2 over 150.3 equals 18.1 degrees. Because both components of Vector D are negative, Doug pulls in the third quadrant. His force is therefore directed 18.1 degrees south of west. The conclusion. To keep the toy in equilibrium, Doug must pull with a force of magnitude D equals 158.1 nuutens directed 18.1 degrees south of west. Doug's force has the same magnitude as the resultant force from the other three dogs, but points in the opposite direction. So the net force on the toy is zero. The problem. Find the magnitude of the Vector C that satisfies the vector equation 2 Vector A minus 6 Vector B plus 3 Vector C equals 2 j hat. Where the known vectors are Vector A equals I hat minus 2 k hat and Vector B equals negative j hat plus 1 half k hat. The worked solution follows. The model. We model the given expression as a three-dimensional vector equation written in the standard Cartesian basis. The unit vectors I hat, j hat and k hat represent mutually perpendicular directions. The unknown vector is determined by comparing matching components along the three coordinate axes. Once its components are identified, its magnitude is found from the three-dimensional length of the vector. The math. The goal is to solve the vector equation for the unknown vector C. To isolate Vector C, the known vector terms are moved to the right side and then the equation is divided by 3. 2 Vector A minus 6 Vector B plus 3 Vector C equals 2 j hat. 3 Vector C equals 2 j hat minus 2 Vector A plus 6 Vector B. Vector C equals 2 over 3 j hat minus 2 over 3 Vector A plus 2 Vector B. The known vectors are then inserted into the expression for Vector C so that matching unit vector components can be combined. Vector C equals 2 over 3 j hat minus 2 over 3 times I hat minus 2 k hat plus 2 times negative j hat plus 1 half k hat. Vector C equals negative 2 over 3 i hat plus 2 over 3 minus 2 j hat plus 4 over 3 plus 1 k hat. Vector C equals negative 2 over 3 i hat minus 4 over 3 j hat plus 7 over 3 k hat. The scalar components of Vector C are therefore C sub X equals negative 2 over 3 C sub Y equals negative 4 over 3 C sub Z equals 7 over 3. The magnitude of Vector C is found by applying the three-dimensional magnitude formula to these components. The magnitude of Vector C equals square root of C sub X to the power of 2 plus C sub Y to the power of 2 plus C sub Z to the power of 2. Vector C equals square root of negative 2 over 3 squared plus negative 4 over 3 squared plus 7 over 3 squared equals square root of 23 over 3. The conclusion, the Vector C is Vector C equals negative 2 over 3 i hat minus 4 over 3 j hat plus 7 over 3 k hat. And its magnitude is Vector C equals square root of 23 over 3 is approximately equal to 2.77. This result follows from first solving for the Vector components and then applying the three-dimensional magnitude formula. Frequent mistake. A frequent mistake in problems like this is mixing up Vector components with magnitudes. i hat, j hat and k hat are directional basis vectors, not numbers. In Python, they correspond to array positions, not separate variables. Writing a line like C equals the square root of C X squared plus C Y squared plus C Z squared before identifying the components will lead to errors. Always solve for the Vector first, then compute its magnitude. Sometimes we need to know just the direction of a Vector, such as the direction of a magnetic field at some point or the direction of motion of an object. The unit vector gives a vector its direction and is dimensionless, which means it has no physical units. When the vector lies along one of the axes in the coordinate system, finding the direction is simple. Its direction is either parallel or anti-parallel to that coordinate axis. For example, the direction of the vector d equals negative 5 i hat meters is the unit vector d hat equals negative i hat. The general rule for finding the unit vector v hat of a vector v is to divide the vector by its magnitude. V hat equals vector v over v. The problem. A military convoy moves through unknown territory with velocity vector v equals 4.0 i hat plus 3.0 j hat plus 0.10 k hat kilometers per hour. What is the unit vector that gives the direction of the convoy's motion? The worked solution follows. The model. We model the convoy's velocity as a three-dimensional vector with east, north, and upward components. The direction of motion is represented by a unit vector parallel to the velocity vector. A unit vector describes direction only and has no physical units. To find the unit vector, the velocity vector is scaled so that its magnitude becomes 1 while its direction remains unchanged. The math. The unit vector in the direction of the motion is found by dividing the velocity vector by its magnitude. V hat equals vector v over magnitude of vector v. The magnitude of the velocity vector is determined from its three rectangular components. Magnitude of vector v equals square root of v sub x to the power of 2 plus v sub y to the power of 2 plus v sub z to the power of 2. Equals square root of 4.0 squared plus 3.0 squared plus 0.10 squared kilometers per hour. Equals square root of 25.01 kilometers per hour is approximately equal to 5.0 kilometers per hour. Dividing each component of vector v by this magnitude gives the corresponding component of the unit vector. V hat equals 0.80i hat plus 0.60j hat plus 0.020k hat over 5.0. Equals 0.80i hat plus 0.60j hat plus 0.020k hat. The conclusion. The unit vector describing the direction of the convoys motion is v hat equals 0.80i hat plus 0.60j hat plus 0.020k hat. This vector has magnitude 1 and describes only the direction of the convoys motion, not its speed. Warning. A frequent mistake is to divide only one component of the vector by the magnitude. A unit vector must preserve the direction of the original vector, so every component must be divided by the same magnitude. Forgetting this produces a vector that no longer points in the correct direction.

The math. The goal is to solve the vector equation for the unknown vector C. To isolate Vector C, the known vector terms are moved to the right side and then the equation is divided by 3.
2 Vector A minus 6 Vector B plus 3 Vector C equals 2 j hat. 3 Vector C equals 2 j hat minus 2 Vector A plus 6 Vector B.
Vector C equals 2 over 3 j hat minus 2 over 3 Vector A plus 2 Vector B.
The known vectors are then inserted into the expression for Vector C so that matching unit vector components can be combined.
Vector C equals 2 over 3 j hat minus 2 over 3 times I hat minus 2 k hat plus 2 times negative j hat plus 1 half k hat.
Vector C equals negative 2 over 3 i hat plus 2 over 3 minus 2 j hat plus 4 over 3 plus 1 k hat.
Vector C equals negative 2 over 3 i hat minus 4 over 3 j hat plus 7 over 3 k hat.
The scalar components of Vector C are therefore C sub X equals negative 2 over 3 C sub Y equals negative 4 over 3 C sub Z equals 7 over 3.
The magnitude of Vector C is found by applying the three-dimensional magnitude formula to these components.
The magnitude of Vector C equals square root of C sub X to the power of 2 plus C sub Y to the power of 2 plus C sub Z to the power of 2.
Vector C equals square root of negative 2 over 3 squared plus negative 4 over 3 squared plus 7 over 3 squared equals square root of 23 over 3.
The conclusion, the Vector C is Vector C equals negative 2 over 3 i hat minus 4 over 3 j hat plus 7 over 3 k hat.
And its magnitude is Vector C equals square root of 23 over 3 is approximately equal to 2.77.
This result follows from first solving for the Vector components and then applying the three-dimensional magnitude formula.
Frequent mistake. A frequent mistake in problems like this is mixing up Vector components with magnitudes.
i hat, j hat and k hat are directional basis vectors, not numbers. In Python, they correspond to array positions, not separate variables.
Writing a line like C equals the square root of C X squared plus C Y squared plus C Z squared before identifying the components will lead to errors.
Always solve for the Vector first, then compute its magnitude.
Sometimes we need to know just the direction of a Vector, such as the direction of a magnetic field at some point or the direction of motion of an object.
The unit vector gives a vector its direction and is dimensionless, which means it has no physical units.
When the vector lies along one of the axes in the coordinate system, finding the direction is simple. Its direction is either parallel or anti-parallel to that coordinate axis.
For example, the direction of the vector d equals negative 5 i hat meters is the unit vector d hat equals negative i hat.
The general rule for finding the unit vector v hat of a vector v is to divide the vector by its magnitude. V hat equals vector v over v.
The problem. A military convoy moves through unknown territory with velocity vector v equals 4.0 i hat plus 3.0 j hat plus 0.10 k hat kilometers per hour.
What is the unit vector that gives the direction of the convoy's motion? The worked solution follows. The model.
We model the convoy's velocity as a three-dimensional vector with east, north, and upward components. The direction of motion is represented by a unit vector parallel to the velocity vector.
A unit vector describes direction only and has no physical units. To find the unit vector, the velocity vector is scaled so that its magnitude becomes 1 while its direction remains unchanged.
The math. The unit vector in the direction of the motion is found by dividing the velocity vector by its magnitude. V hat equals vector v over magnitude of vector v.

The magnitude of the velocity vector is determined from its three rectangular components. Magnitude of vector v equals square root of v sub x to the power of 2 plus v sub y to the power of 2 plus v sub z to the power of 2.
Equals square root of 4.0 squared plus 3.0 squared plus 0.10 squared kilometers per hour. Equals square root of 25.01 kilometers per hour is approximately equal to 5.0 kilometers per hour.
Dividing each component of vector v by this magnitude gives the corresponding component of the unit vector. V hat equals 0.80i hat plus 0.60j hat plus 0.020k hat over 5.0.
Equals 0.80i hat plus 0.60j hat plus 0.020k hat. The conclusion. The unit vector describing the direction of the convoys motion is v hat equals 0.80i hat plus 0.60j hat plus 0.020k hat.
This vector has magnitude 1 and describes only the direction of the convoys motion, not its speed.

Warning. A frequent mistake is to divide only one component of the vector by the magnitude. A unit vector must preserve the direction of the original vector, so every component must be divided by the same magnitude.
Forgetting this produces a vector that no longer points in the correct direction.
